newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's Labour rejects Alliance pre-poll olive branch.
newsitem.headline: NZ's Labour rejects Alliance pre-poll olive branch.

text.p: New Zealand Alliance Party leader Jim Anderton on Wednesday offered an olive branch to the Labour Party, saying that if the parties of the left did not reach a pre-election arrangement, New Zealand would continue its experience of right-wing government.
"We're not talking about coalition before the election," Anderton told Radio New Zealand.
"Labour can fight on its policies and we'll fight on ours. But what if none of us get enough to govern? What will be the policies of the potential coalition?

"The majority of the people of New Zealand I am sure do not want the possibilty of this right-wing government," he said, referring to the possibility of a National-led, right-of-centre coalition government.
But Labour Party leader Helen Clark ruled out any pre-election talks with the Alliance, saying Anderton's offer was a "stunt".

"I've lost count of the number of times I have heard from the media that Mr Anderton has a confidential letter coming to me wanting private talks. It is a stunt. Winston Peters called it a stunt earlier. He's right," Clark told the radio station.
She said Labour would not talk with potential coalition partners until after the election.
"I've consistently said that after the election, Labour will be the major opposition party, and will be in a position to reach out to other people to form a government.
"What I find very, very unhelpful now is Mr Anderton's ultimatum that unless you conclude some kind of arrangement with him now, he will not play ball afterwards.
"Frankly I think that dashes the hopes of the majority of New Zealand voters who are looking for change of government," Clark said.
Anderton has said he will not compromise Alliance policies after the election and was critical of Labour's refusal to identify its most likely coalition partners.
"Labour says they won't go into coalition with National, the Alliance says we won't go into coalition with National, who does that leave for goodness sake?
"Is the Labour Party going to go into coalition with ACT? If they're not, then the Alliance is the only possibility," Anderton said.
"So why don't we say that publicly so people know before the election. They've got a right to know before they vote."
He said Clark should not reject the offer because many voters were telling him the two must get together to stop a National-led coalition taking power.

But Clark said Anderton's polices, especially the Aliiance's economic stance, were too rigid. She called on the Alliance to support Labour after the election, but dismissed as "ridiculous" the suggestion that Labour might be in a position of supporting the Alliance.
"The Alliance is not going to be in a position to form a government," she said.

"My request to Mr Anderton is: 'get on with your campaign. After the election you will have some MPs in parliament, and please then look at the possibility of giving Labour a vote of confidence to form a government'.

"We're not saying you have to come into it, and I don't think that's his preferred position in any case, but if he is going to use his block of votes to block a change of government, then I think the public need to have that spelt out very clearly."
--Wellington Newsroom (64 4) 4734746
